title: Super Typhoon Bavi strikes US Pacific islands with pummeling winds
byline: Howling winds and lashing rains battered Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands as super typhoon Bavi made landfall on Monday.

title: Warehouse containing 4.2 million kg of sugar sealed in Peliyagoda
byline: A warehouse in Peliyagoda belonging to a major sugar importer was raided yesterday (6) after authorities uncovered an alleged operation to repackage expired sugar and release it to the market at lower prices

title: Foreign Employment Bureau loses Rs. 615m over untrained workers: Deputy Minister
byline: The Sri Lanka Bureau of Foreign Employment (SLBFE) has incurred losses of Rs. 615 million due to untrained Sri Lankan nationals leaving the country for overseas employment, Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Employment Arun Hemachandra told Parliament today.

title: Government should accept responsibility: Opposition
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake, the subject minister and the government as a whole should accept the responsibility for the clash at Negombo Prison, which has left 26 people dead, the opposition said yesterday.

title: Girl raped by three young men including brother
byline: A 12-year-old schoolgirl of Bogahakumbura in Welimada has been raped by three young men at times, and one of them is her 21-year-old brother.

title: CID launches probe into Negombo Prison unrest; Key inmate transferred to Boossa
byline: The Criminal Investigation Department (CID) has launched an investigation into the unrest at Negombo Prison, deploying three investigation teams to inspect the facility and question those involved.

title: GMOA raises alarm over hidden dengue cases
byline: The Government Medical Officers’ Association (GMOA) has raised concerns that the actual number of dengue infections in Sri Lanka could be significantly higher than the officially reported figures, warning that the country may be witnessing the early stages of a major outbreak similar to the 2017 epidemic.

title: Carnage!: How did prisoners access guns?
byline: In what appeared to be yet another deadly outbreak of rioting, 19 inmates and seven prison officers were killed, and around 100 were injured in the Negombo jail yesterday. Initially, riots broke out between two drug gangs on Sunday, and the confrontation rapidly spiralled into one of Sri Lanka’s deadliest prison riots in recent history, resulting in heavy casualties and exposing serious security concerns.

title: Belgium thump USA to reach quarter-finals and end co-hosts’ World Cup dream
byline: Charles de Ketelaere scored twice for Belgium as the United States became the third and final co-host to be knocked out of the World Cup.

title: Ronaldo’s World Cup career ends in tears
byline: One of football’s great careers will finish without the biggest prize after Cristiano Ronaldo’s final World Cup match for Portugal ended with a 1-0 last-16 defeat by Spain.

title: Iran fires missiles at commercial ships in Strait of Hormuz
byline: Iran’s Revolutionary Guards fired at least two missiles at commercial ships transiting through the Strait of Hormuz on Monday night, Axios reported, citing two U.S. officials.

title: 734 inmates transfered to other prisons: Minister
byline: A total of 734 inmates, who were involved in the clash at the Negombo prison have been transfered to other prisons, Minister of Justice and National Integration Harshana Nanayakkara said today.

title: Parliament to take up debate on prison clash today
byline: Parliament is to take up a debate on the Negombo prison clashes today from 3.30 pm to 6.30 pm, Speaker Jagath Wickramaratne announced today.

title: Court of Appeal upholds death sentence in Galle electrocution murder case
byline: The Court of Appeal has upheld the conviction and death sentence imposed on a man found guilty of murdering his neighbour by electrocuting him with illegally connected live electrical wires surrounding his property in Galle.

title: Kananathan congratulates Ethiopia”s Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed on electoral victory
byline: Former diplomat Ambassador Kananathan, who has maintained a close and long-standing relationship with Ethiopian Prime Minister and Chairman of the Prosperity Party Dr. Abiy Ahmed, has extended his heartfelt congratulations following the Prosperity Party’s decisive victory in Ethiopia’s parliamentary elections.

title: Power set shortage cuts KKS intercity to four days
byline: The daily Intercity Express train operating between Mount Lavinia and Kankesanthurai (KKS) will be limited to four days a week from July 10, due to a shortage of power sets, the Railway Station Master’s Association said.

title: Government refutes claims of removing security assigned to political leaders
byline: Deputy Minister of Public Security and Parliamentary Affairs Sunil Watagala refuted claims that security provided to political leaders has been removed.

title: Moratuwa University temporarily closed over dengue risk
byline: The University of Moratuwa has been temporarily closed for two weeks due to a dengue risk, university authorities said.

title: Negombo Prison unrest: Death toll climbs to 27
byline: The death toll from the violent unrest at the Negombo Prison has risen to 27 after another inmate who was injured in the clashes died while undergoing treatment at the Negombo Hospital, Police said today.

title: Court upholds eight-year jail term on man for sexually abusing six-year-old child
byline: The Court of Appeal upheld the conviction and eight-year rigorous imprisonment imposed on a man who had sexually abused a six-year-old girl in Moneragala in 2010.

title: Tanker set ablaze after being struck in the Strait of Hormuz as Iran mourns Khamenei
byline: A tanker traveling off the coast of Oman in the Strait of Hormuz caught on fire early Tuesday morning after being struck by a projectile, the British military said.

title: Govt. launches relief programme for ornamental fish breeders affected by Cyclone Ditwah
byline: The Government has launched a special relief programme to support small-scale ornamental fish breeders affected by Cyclone Ditwah, with Fisheries, Aquatic and Ocean Resources Minister Ramalingam Chandrasekar directing officials to import new breeding stock every three months to strengthen the industry.

title: Opposition seeks urgent parliamentary debate on Negombo prison clashes
byline: Thirty-one Opposition MPs have submitted a motion to Speaker Jagath Wickramaratne seeking an urgent adjournment debate on the recent clashes at Negombo Prison.

title: How did prisoners access guns?
byline: In what appeared to be yet another deadly outbreak of rioting, 19 inmates and seven prison officers were killed, and around 100 were injured in the Negombo jail yesterday. Initially, riots broke out between two drug gangs on Sunday, and the confrontation rapidly spiralled into one of Sri Lanka’s deadliest prison riots in recent history, resulting in heavy casualties and exposing serious security concerns.

title: No prior intelligence received on Negombo Prison violence: Prisons Chief
byline: Authorities had received no prior intelligence indicating that a violent incident was likely to occur at Negombo Prison, Acting Commissioner General of Prisons Prasad Hemantha Kumara has confirmed, as multiple investigations continue into the deadly unrest.

title: Kerawalapitiya industrial zone road left in disrepair despite strategic importance
byline: The main access road leading from the Kerawalapitiya Expressway exit to the Elakanda Junction, which serves the Kerawalapitiya Industrial Estate, has fallen into a state of disrepair, with residents and businesses alleging that no government has taken steps to properly maintain it.

title: Thalatha calls for Harshana’s resignation over Negombo prison clash
byline: Justice and National Integration Minister Harshana Nanayakkara should resign from his post to show that he is taking responsibility for his actions, United National Party (UNP) General Secretary Thalatha Athukorala said.

title: Prisons Dept. pays tribute to seven officers killed in Negombo Prison unrest
byline: The Department of Prisons has paid tribute to the seven prison officers who lost their lives during the recent unrest at Negombo Prison, describing them as ’’heroes who sacrificed their lives in duty.’’

title: Namal-led group launches “A Team – Next Wave”
byline: Opposition MPs Namal Rajapaksa, Rohitha Abeygunawardena, Anuradha Jayaratne, D. V. Chanaka and Chanaka Madugoda on Tuesday launched a new political platform titled “A Team – Next Wave”, saying it aims to unite opposition voices both inside and outside Parliament.

title: Zelensky to press Nato for air defence systems after intense Russian strikes
byline: Ukraine’s president plans to use the Nato meeting in Turkey to urge Kyiv’s allies to deliver the air defence systems it urgently needs to protect it from escalating Russian attacks.

title: Namal’s Krrish deal case fixed for trial
byline: The controversial Krrish deal case filed against Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) Parliamentarian Namal Rajapaksa was today fixed for trial by the Colombo High Court.

title: Rs. 1 mn compensation for patients who lost eyesight during Keheliya’s tenure
byline: The Government has decided to pay compensation of Rs. 1 million each to four patients who lost their eyesight or suffered vision impairment following eye surgeries after the use of Prednisolone Acetate eye drops at government hospitals during the tenure of former Health Minister Keheliya Rambukwella.

title: Peradeniya University added to Kandy wastewater project
byline: The Government has approved the expansion of the Kandy Urban Wastewater Management Project to include the premises of the University of Peradeniya.

title: Rohana Randombage appointed Director General of Sustainable Energy Authority
byline: Chartered Engineer Rohana Randombage has been appointed as the new Director General of the Sri Lanka Sustainable Energy Authority.

title: Women’s T20 World Cup 2026 Rewrites Record Books
byline: Australia’s seventh ICC Women’s T20 World Cup title capped a record-breaking 2026 tournament, with players and teams setting new milestones throughout the biggest edition in the event’s history.

title: Cabinet approves VMS for 1,500 fishing vessels
byline: The Cabinet has approved a proposal to expand the Vessel Monitoring System (VMS) to cover around 1,500 multi-day and one-day fishing vessels operating in Sri Lanka.

title: Pilot bus sector clustering programme approved
byline: The Government has approved a pilot programme to introduce a bus sector clustering system to improve public transport services and address existing issues in the bus sector.

title: Former Afghanistan fast bowler Shapoor Zadran passes away
byline: Former Afghanistan fast bowler Shapoor Zadran has died in India after battling an illness. He had been undergoing treatment at a hospital in India for some time.

title: Kananathan congratulates Ethiopia’s Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed on electoral victory
byline: Former diplomat Ambassador Kananathan, who has maintained a close and long-standing relationship with Ethiopian Prime Minister and Chairman of the Prosperity Party Dr. Abiy Ahmed, has extended his heartfelt congratulations following the Prosperity Party’s decisive victory in Ethiopia’s parliamentary elections.

title: SLPP urges Sajith to unite democratic parties against judge retirement extension
byline: The Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) has called on Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa to convene a meeting of all democratic political parties to oppose the government’s reported move to extend the retirement age of Supreme Court judges.

title: Blasts rock Damascus during Macron visit
byline: Bombs exploded near the hotel where Emmanuel Macron was staying in Syria on Tuesday, a security source said, but the French president did not hear ​the explosions, the Elysee said, and he met Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa ​soon afterwards.

title: China sentences official to death for taking $325m in bribes
byline: A court in eastern China has sentenced a former city official to death for taking more than 2.2bn yuan ($325m; £243m) in bribes over 30 years.

title: UN calls for prison reforms after Negombo Prison violence
byline: The United Nations Resident Coordinator in Sri Lanka has called for renewed investment in the country’s prison system following the deadly violence at the Negombo Prison, while welcoming the appointment of an independent committee to investigate the incident.

title: Zimbabwean football star survives gun attack in South Africa
byline: Zimbabwean footballer Divine Lunga has survived a gun attack in Johannesburg, South African police have said.

title: Navy joins dengue prevention drive for third consecutive day
byline: The Sri Lanka Navy has continued its support for the national dengue prevention campaign for the third consecutive day, joining efforts to strengthen the ’’Towards a Dengue-Free Colombo’’ initiative.

title: Three platforms reopened at Colombo Fort after train derailment
byline: Three of the four platforms blocked following a train derailment at the Colombo Fort Railway Station have now been reopened after the affected train was rerouted and moved to Maradana Railway Station, railway authorities said.

title: Committee appointed to probe Negombo prison unrest
byline: The government has appointed a three-member Committee of Inquiry to conduct a comprehensive investigation into the unrest that erupted at Negombo Prison on July 5 and 6.

title: CSE extends decline as cautious investors await earnings season
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange continued its downward movement on Tuesday, with both benchmark indices closing lower as investors remained cautious ahead of the upcoming quarterly earnings season. The market opened on a negative note and gradually moved lower throughout the session, with subdued turnover and share volumes reflecting limited investor participation and a lack of strong market conviction.

title: Minister visits injured prison officers and inmates at National Hospital
byline: Health Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa today visited the National Hospital of Sri Lanka to review the condition of those injured in the recent unrest at the Negombo Prison.

title: Indonesia, India announce long-range missile deal
byline: India will supply Indonesia with long-range missiles, an Indian official said on Tuesday (Jul 7) as their leaders agreed to deepen ties in defence, critical minerals and other areas.

title: Train derails at Colombo Fort, disrupting rail services
byline: A train scheduled to depart from Colombo Fort Railway Station for Rambukkana at 4.45 p.m. derailed at around 4.50 p.m. today while approaching its designated platform.

title: Officer opened fire to prevent prison breach, says Acting Prisons Chief
byline: Acting Commissioner General of Prisons Prasad Hemantha Kumara has defended the actions of an officer seen opening fire through a gate during the recent unrest at Negombo Prison, saying the officer acted to prevent a catastrophic prison breach and protect prison officers trapped inside.

title: Woman suspected of Monaco bombing found shot dead near Kyiv
byline: A woman suspected of carrying out last week’s bomb attack in Monaco that seriously injured a Ukraine-born business tycoon has been found shot dead near Kyiv, in the latest twist in a case that has shaken the wealthy Mediterranean principality.

title: Central Bank warns public against urgency-based online scams
byline: The Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL) has urged the public to remain vigilant against online scams that create a false sense of urgency to trick victims into sharing personal and financial information.

title: Zimbabwean football star survives gun attack in South Africa
byline: Zimbabwean footballer Divine Lunga has survived a gun attack in Johannesburg, South African police have said.
